items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: I just used to take the parts of an orchestra, either by Arthur Lang or Walter Paul or Don Redman... I started studying what they called 'stock arrangements' -- arrangements by Don Redman, Archie Blyer, Arthur Lang, Walter Paul

ctx.x: at a very early stage in your arranging career. Can you sort of describe that process?

Oh. Well, all I meant by that was that I didn't know anything about making a score; I hadn't studied orchestrating or instrumentation or composition at that time, and I just used to take the parts of an orchestra, either by Arthur Lang or Walter Paul or Don Redman, or, what are some of the other names? Archie Bleyer, who came a little later.
